method: Bridges: every features.json bridge (deck ends = the carrier way ends), plus every crossing of a road (not a path) or rail line over a river or stream with no record of the same kind within 40 m (deck ends 10 m either side). deckH = max(mean end height, ground + 2 m); hwAt from flood.json, interpolated. Road segments: each road split at tile edges and at vertices shared with another road, then into equal pieces of at most 250 m. inWood = at least half the 10 m samples inside a woods polygon; band = deepest band sampled (3 under a trapped lake at spill). Storm and survivors are hand-picked in Tools/worldgen/decisions.ts. Damage: each bridge falls with a logistic probability in depth below the mark (about 0.1 above, 0.9 at 40 m below, 0.95 deeper, plus a small bump near the storm centre); survivors stand. Each road segment is blocked with a probability by band and woods (within 20 m of a wood counts as beside it): see Tools/worldgen/rules/damage.ts. Rolled once with a fixed seed. Tile lists are empty.

storm.why: Sourton Down, SX 548 935: worst over the Meldon valley and the west edge of the moor; Okehampton gets the fringe.

survivors.name: Meldon Viaduct
survivors.why: Open wrought-iron lattice piers and spans, far below the mark: the wave went through it, not against it. The dramatic survivor.

survivors.name: A30 East Okement bridge
survivors.why: Modern concrete dual carriageway, the one way east over the East Okement once the town bridges are gone.
